header:
Date: 2027-11-15
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Chris Turner (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Sable CTO), Priya Patel (Sable Head of MLOps), Miguel Santos (Sable Procurement)
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Sable is evaluating upgrading to a Dedicated 8-GPU pool and expanding Redwood service to eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Discussed sizing, cost tradeoffs (latency vs cost), compliance (SOC2, KMS), and contract term extension. Agreed to run benchmarks in eu-west-1 and circulate pricing + contract amendment.
topics: Capacity upgrade: Dedicated 8-GPU pool sizing and autoscaling
Additional regions: eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 onboarding
Contract extension: 12-month amendment, billing and SLAs
transcript:
[00:00:05] Chris (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:00:11] Jordan (CTO): Jordan here.
[00:00:13] Priya (Head of MLOps): Priya on.
[00:00:15] Miguel (Procurement): Miguel here.
[00:00:18] Maya (SE): Maya from Redwood, good to see you all.
[00:00:22] Chris: Cool, agenda - renewal timeline, capacity needs, region expansion, and any compliance/legal asks. Jordan, want to kick off with where you are?
[00:00:34] Jordan: Yeah, quick overview - overall happy with current throughput on hosted but we are hitting tail latency on peak windows, especially for multi-turn chat. our product team is asking for predictable p99 under 300ms which we aren't always hitting. We're planning a Q1 product push so we need headroom.
[00:00:55] Priya: To add, our daytime peaks are around 1.2k concurrent requests, avg seq len 350 tokens, and we need retention for 30 days of logs for audit. Also want eu-west for GDPR reasons.
[00:01:12] Chris: Got it. sounds like Dedicated could help with predictability. Maya, quick primer on Dedicated sizing?
[00:01:20] Maya: Sure, Dedicated 8-GPU pool should give you the p99 headroom, assuming we tune batching and prefix caching. important to note quantization profiles matter - if you go 4-bit you reduce GPU memory and can get more concurrency but some evals show small quality delta.
[00:01:40] Jordan: What's the tradeoff on latency if we enable larger batch sizes? we can't sacrifice tail.
[00:01:45] Maya: Right, batching reduces cost but increases latency; with continuous batching we can keep average latency low and still meet p99 if we set the batching thresholds and timeouts properly. we usually set a strict p99 guardrail for customer SLOs.
[00:02:03] Miguel: On procurement, timeline - if we sign amendment this month we need invoices and PO by end of next week. is that doable?
[00:02:10] Chris: We can aim for that; I'll send updated pricing today.
[00:02:15] Jordan: Also regional question: we want eu-west-1 for data residency and ap-southeast-1 for latency to AP users. what's the onboarding time for a new region?
[00:02:25] Maya: For Dedicated in a new region there are a few steps - capacity reservation, networking/VPC peering, and compliance checks if you want private control plane. Typical lead time is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity availability. for eu-west we've had recent capacity but ap-southeast may need longer.
[00:02:45] Priya: Do we get separate KMS per region or global key? security team asks about HSM support.
[00:02:50] Maya: We support customer-managed KMS keys per region and can integrate with HSM-backed masters. we'll include the KMS notes in the docs.
[00:02:58] Jordan: Good. How about audit logs retention and SSO? we need SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[00:03:05] Chris: Redwood supports SAML SSO, SCIM, and detailed audit logs. We'll share the SOC 2 and architecture diagram after.
[00:03:12] Miguel: On pricing, we need a committed monthly spend model for budgeting - is there a reserved capacity discount?
[00:03:19] Chris: Yes, reserved capacity (Dedicated) comes with tiered discounts for monthly/annual commits. we can show a 12-month and 24-month price.
[00:03:26] Jordan: Are there fallbacks if Dedicated saturates? like autoscaling to hosted or fallback model variants?
[00:03:31] Maya: Yes, smart routing can failover to hosted pool or a lower-cost model variant, configurable by policy. but for strict compliance you may want private-only, in which case fallbacks are limited.
[00:03:44] Priya: Another question - do you support KV cache migration across versions? we do a lot of session pinning.
[00:03:50] Maya: We have KV cache management in runtime; warmup strategies for rollouts and we can snapshot caches during version upgrades. there may be rebuild windows but we minimize disruption.
[00:04:03] Jordan: Great. can we run a benchmark with our exact prompts in eu-west-1? we want p95/p99 and cost per 1M tokens.
[00:04:10] Maya: Absolutely. we'll run a benchmark. need sample prompts and a test harness - we can take that from Priya.
[00:04:18] Priya: I'll share a dataset and example load profile.
[00:04:21] Chris: For contract, you're asking for 12 months with an option to expand after 6?
[00:04:25] Jordan: That's the idea - commit to the capacity for 12 months with a mid-term review at 6 months to optionally add regions.
[00:04:32] Miguel: Legal will want an SLA section with credits, egress estimates, and termination terms.
[00:04:38] Chris: We'll include SLA language and estimated egress. I'll loop in legal on the amendment.
[00:04:42] Jordan: Any blockers on data residency for EU?
[00:04:46] Maya: Only if you need a private control plane - that adds a few days for VPC setup and review, but we can do private or hosted dedicated in-region.
[00:04:55] Priya: Regarding model quantization, can you share recommended profiles for our workload? we saw drift in some generation quality tests when moving to 4-bit.
[00:05:03] Maya: We'll share a quantization recommendation doc. usually we run evals on your prompt set to measure quality delta. sometimes a 4-bit with mixed precision works well; depends on model family.
[00:05:16] Jordan: On monitoring, do you provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards?
[00:05:21] Chris: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost, tracing hooks and rollout controls. we'll send screenshots and access to a demo tenant.
[00:05:33] Miguel: Procurement question - do you accept consolidated invoicing across regions?
[00:05:37] Chris: We can consolidate billing or split by region depending on the contract setup; we'll propose both options.
[00:05:45] Priya: For the benchmark, what tokenization are you using? we use a custom tokenizer pipeline.
[00:05:50] Maya: We can run with your tokenizer as long as you supply the tokenization step. otherwise we use our standard byte-pair tokenizer which we note in cost calcs.
[00:05:59] Jordan: Any notable competitors or features to be aware of?
[00:06:02] Chris: Customers compare us to Lambda Labs for self-hosted, Anthropic for model stack, and AWS Bedrock for region coverage. our differentiator is unified runtime, predictable cost controls, and rollout tooling.
[00:06:14] Miguel: Timeline check - if we do benchmarking this week and agree, could we have amendment signed by Nov 24?
[00:06:20] Chris: We'll push for that - it's tight but possible.
[00:06:24] Priya: On security docs - please include SOC 2, encryption at rest/in transit, and KMS details.
[00:06:30] Maya: Noted, I'll attach the security pack.
[00:06:34] Chris: ok let's go through next steps and owners.
[00:06:36] Jordan: sounds good.
[00:06:39] [Silence / minor crosstalk 00:06:40-00:07:00]
[00:07:05] Chris: Recap: Redwood to send updated pricing and contract amendment draft; Maya to run benchmarks in eu-west with Priya's test harness; Jordan to share traffic profiles; Miguel to share procurement timeline.
[00:07:20] Priya: I'll upload the prompt set and a simple load script to the shared folder by EOD.
[00:07:25] Miguel: I'll get legal and procurement contacts to you by Friday.
[00:07:29] Chris: Great. Anything else from the Sable side?
[00:07:33] Jordan: No, thanks.
[00:07:35] Chris: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the pricing spreadsheet.
[00:07:40] Maya: Thanks all.
[00:07:42] Miguel: Thanks.
[00:07:44] [Call ends - total duration ~45 minutes]

Note: transcription contains a few minor speaker mislabels and occasional filler words, typical of automated meeting transcripts.
